incidents.name: DEI token burnFrom reversed allowance lookup
incidents.notes: The DEI implementation deployed on 2023-04-16 wrote the allowance update inside burnFrom() with the owner and spender arguments transposed, so calling burnFrom(victim, 0) granted the caller an unlimited allowance over the victim and let the attacker transferFrom every DEI holder that had ever approved the token.

sources.ref: onchain review: DEI proxy 0xde1e704dae0b4051e80dabb26ab6ad6c12262da0 created 2022-11-15 by 0x18b4287fa4155efd149aece678a75bbd69ede0b8 (Deus deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x189cf534de3097c08b6beaf6eb2b9179dab122d1; 4 EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last on 2023-04-16 to implementation 0xbc1b62db243b51dabcd9540473324f36e094ec55 - that upgrade introduced the flaw, giving a 19.3-day code age; lossUsd is the Arbitrum share (~$5M) of the ~$6.5M taken across Arbitrum, BSC and Ethereum

incidents.name: DEUS DeiLenderSolidex spot-price collateral valuation
incidents.notes: DeiLenderSolidex valued its USDC/DEI Solidly LP collateral from the pair's live reserves, so a 150M USDC flash loan that skewed the pair let the attacker borrow DEI far in excess of the collateral's real worth.

sources.ref: onchain review on Fantom over a public RPC (no explorer creation API): binary search over eth_getCode places DeiLenderSolidex 0x8D643d954798392403eeA19dB8108f595bB8B730 first having code at block 35230623, 2022-04-04T18:00:15Z; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events before the incident, so the executing code was 23.9 days old. Attack-tx sender 0xc564ee9f21ed8a2d8e7e76c085740d5e4c5fafbe. Loss $13 million per the DeFiHackLabs 2022 index entry for this PoC.
